question: A manager has asked Claude for two different versions of a strategy update and must choose one for a board pack. What should she do first?
options: A) Ask Claude which of its two versions is the stronger and take that recommendation forward.
B) Read both versions through carefully and pick whichever one reads more persuasively to her.
C) Merge the two versions into one document so that nothing useful from either is left behind.
D) Write down what the board needs to take from the update before she reads either version.
correct_answers: D) Write down what the board needs to take from the update before she reads either version.
explanations: Incorrect. Claude has not been told what this board needs, so its preference is about writing quality rather than fit.
Incorrect. Persuasiveness to the writer is not the test; a polished draft can still fail to give the board what it needs to decide.
Incorrect. Merging before criteria exist produces a longer document that serves the board less well than either original.
Correct. Without stated criteria a comparison collapses into which draft reads more nicely. Setting the audience's needs down first makes the choice a judgment rather than a preference.
